WHAT LANDED: Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean, sorry-free. The (f, hf) certificate is FACTORED, and its
bookkeeping half is discharged unconditionally:
  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map        -- open immersion of SCHEMES is one of PRESHEAVES
  restrictChart f V                          -- the chart map restricted to an open of its source
  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart     -- the COMPOSITION half of hf
  chartHom_restrictChart                     -- so LocallyOfFiniteType is inherited by restrictions
The restriction is what makes any of this possible: IsOpenImmersion.presheaf of the UNRESTRICTED
Abel chart is FALSE (fibres are the projective spaces |D|), and chartLocus now exists to restrict to.

THE GATE, corrected again. This node said CERT-Sigma-gated: a DivRepGlobalData term plus the
shifted-datum constructor. Two updates:
 1. divRep is no longer the binding half. ajcr-divrep published DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy
    (Picard/DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:306, sorry-free, rooted) as the public endpoint, and it is
    exactly the RepresentableBy shape abelSigmaChart already consumes. Nothing on my side needs to
    change to consume it.
 2. The shifted-datum constructor splits into an INVERSE half (landed this session) and a
    MUL/TENSOR half (not landed, needs a common refinement of two basic-open covers plus a
    comparison of the two cechPicClass readings there). The mul/tensor half is the live gate of
    isOpen_chartLocus, and cechPicClass_inv is separately unlanded.

SO THE REMAINING C9b OBLIGATION IS ONE STATEMENT, CHART-U(c): on chartLocus the Abel map is
injective, because the normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2). Feed that
plus openness of the locus into isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart and hf is done. Do NOT read
the composition lemma as reducing C9b to plumbing -- it isolates the plumbing so the mathematics
is visible.

1	# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)
2	
3	Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
4	standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
5	workspace.
6	
7	## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)
8	
9	All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
10	SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
11	freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
13	
14	```bash
15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
24	
25	Archon-Commit: agent
26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
29	```
30	
31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
34	
35	### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed
36	
37	Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
38	was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
39	`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).
40	
41	The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
42	publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
43	The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
44	describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
45	including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
46	the shared index drifts behind.
47	
48	Consequences, all three binding:
49	
50	1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
51	   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
52	2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
53	   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
54	   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
55	   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
56	3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
57	   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
58	   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).
59	
60	Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
61	the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.
62	
63	## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there
64	
65	`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
66	directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
67	that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
68	path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
69	15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
70	
71	```bash
72	LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
73	while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
74	  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
75	  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
76	  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
77	  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
78	    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
79	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
80	      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
81	    fi
82	    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
83	    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
84	       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
85	      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
86	    fi
87	  fi
88	  sleep 10
89	done
90	echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
91	# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
92	```
93	
94	Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
95	- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
96	- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
97	  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
98	  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
99	  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
100	  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.
101	
102	## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
103	
104	uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
105	(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
106	build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
107	retry-looping.
108	
109	## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
110	
111	`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
112	sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
113	in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
114	YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
115	`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
116	other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
117	HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
118	only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
119	root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
120	
121	### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)
122	
123	The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
124	2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
125	worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
126	sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
127	The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
128	i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.
129	
130	So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:
131	
132	> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
133	> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
134	> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
135	> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
136	> usually accompanies it.
137	
138	This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
139	still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
140	warning.
141	
142	**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
143	other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
144	exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards

12	
13	The co-signed brick of `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 (CHART-U(a)) and
14	`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, in the SPLIT form the (a-amendment) binds:
15	
16	> `t ∈ chartLocus c λ` iff for some (equivalently every) finite separable `L/κ(t)`
17	> splitting the collapsed plus class, the honest `L`-class of `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` admits
18	> an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
19	
20	Everything here is over a GENERAL test `T` and an ARBITRARY plus class
21	`λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C T`.  That is what distinguishes it from
22	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean`'s `cechWitnessLocus`, which lives over an affine base
23	and reads an UNTWISTED `CechPic` class; the module header there says so, and this file is
24	the promised general-test article.
25	
26	## The layering, and why the split predicate is a *definition* here and not a disjunction
27	
28	Three separate things had to be joined, and they are joined in three steps:
29	
30	1. `Over.testPoint` (`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`) turns a point `t : T.left` into a
31	   field point `overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ T`, so that `picEtMap C (testPoint t) λ` is the fibre
32	   class of `λ` at `t`.  Without it there is no way to even state the predicate over a
33	   general test.
34	2. `IsSplitWitness` reads a plus class over a FIELD.  A plus class over a field is
35	   `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`, which is *not* an honest Čech class; the
36	   (a-amendment)'s "finite separable `L` splitting the class" is exactly
37	   `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom` (`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:287`)
38	   applied to `E`, after which `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom`
39	   (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:101`) presents the class as `relPicMk` of an honest
40	   Čech class over `C_L`.  The predicate is then the tree's witness predicate on that Čech
41	   class.
42	3. `chartLocus` twists by the chart index `(m, Σ)` — the same twist
43	   `abelDiv · sigmaFamily Σ · (θ^m)⁻¹` that `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`)
44	   applies on the divisor side — and reads step 2 at step 1's field point.
45	
46	The "some (equivalently every)" of the amendment is the honest content: the ∃-form is what
47	one *proves* (coverage produces one splitting, §1.2 step 6), the ∀-form is what one
48	*consumes* (any presenting splitting is a sound test).  Their agreement is
49	`isSplitWitness_iff_forall`, and it rests on
50	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`
51	(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:157`) — the separable-invariance that lane co-owned
52	— together with class-intrinsicity at a fixed field
53	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`, `:177`).  So the definition is stated in
54	the ∃-form and the ∀-form is a theorem, not a second definition.

58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSplitWitness C π μ` — the split witness predicate at a class
59	  `μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)` over a field `K`: some finite separable `L/K` presents `μ`

62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_iff_forall` — the (a-amendment)'s "some (equivalently

64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartTwist C m Σ λ` — the twisted fibre family

109	/-! ## The split witness predicate at a class over a field -/
110	
111	variable (C) in
112	/-- **The split witness predicate** (CHART-U(a) in the `w4-datb` §1.6 (a-amendment)
113	spelling), at a plus class `μ` over a field `K`.
114	
115	A plus class over a field need not be an honest Čech class — it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for
116	an étale cover `E` of `K`.  The amendment's "for some finite separable `L/κ(t)` splitting
117	the collapsed plus class" is this: there is a finite separable extension `L/K` over which
118	`μ` becomes `relPicMk` of an honest Čech class `M` on `C_L`, and `M` admits an effective
119	witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
120	
121	Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
122	because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
123	the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
124	
125	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread
126	
127	The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
128	and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
129	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
130	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
131	on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
132	class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
133	against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
134	condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
135	with it the openness route.
136	
137	Two consequences, both load-bearing:
138	
139	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
140	  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
141	  `deg Z − m·d₁`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `−g`.  It is *not* a
142	  hypothesis of this predicate;
143	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
144	  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
145	  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the
146	  effectivity must be re-supplied at that point.  A lane that reads `IsSplitWitness` as
147	  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/
148	def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
149	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) : Prop :=
150	  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
151	      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
152	      (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
153	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
154	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
155	      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
156	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
157	            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
158	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
159	
160	/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/
161	
162	variable (C) in
163	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
164	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
165	
166	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
167	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
168	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
169	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
170	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
171	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
172	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
173	  lam * sigmaFamily C Z T * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m)⁻¹
174	
175	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
176	degree `deg Z − m·d₁` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
177	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `−g`; the chart-side `chartValue` lands at `n + deg Z − m·d₁`
178	(`degAt_chartValue`, `DivSchemeAbel.lean:368`), so the two agree at `n = 0` — which is why
179	`chartLocus` tests the class `λθ^m(−Σ)` and not `λ` itself. -/
180	theorem degAt_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
181	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T)
182	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
183	    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
184	      = Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z - (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) := by
185	  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
186	    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]
187	  ring

189	/-! ## CHART-U(a): the locus -/
190	
191	variable (C) in
192	/-- **CHART-U(a), `chartLocus`** (`w4-datc` §3.3, co-signed `w4-datb` §1.6): the set of
193	points of a general test `T` at which the twisted fibre class `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` has, after
194	some finite separable splitting of the collapsed plus class at `κ(t)`, an effective witness
195	divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
196	
197	The three layers, each supplied by a named brick:
198	* the *point-to-field-point* passage is `Over.testPoint` (input 0 of this brick — the one
199	  nothing in the tree had);
200	* the *twist* is `chartTwist`, the class-side avatar of `chartValue`;
201	* the *split witness reading over a field* is `IsSplitWitness`.
202	
203	This is the RESERVED name of `Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean`'s header, now defined.  Note it is
204	strictly stronger than `cechWitnessLocus`: general test, twisted class, split predicate. -/
205	def chartLocus (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
206	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) : Set T.left :=
207	  {t : T.left | IsSplitWitness C
208	    (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))}
209	
210	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
211	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left) :
212	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam ↔ IsSplitWitness C
213	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)) :=
214	  Iff.rfl

216	/-! ## The datum-layer reading
217	
218	The witness clause of `IsSplitWitness` is stated on a presenting Čech class over `C_L`.
219	The tree's *engine-facing* predicate is stated on a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum`
220	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`), and
221	the two are joined by `exists_cechPicClass_eq` (every class is presented) plus
222	class-intrinsicity.  This is the seam CHART-U(b) crosses to reach
223	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, so it is recorded here as a lemma of the definition
224	rather than left implicit in the openness proof. -/
225	
226	/-- **The witness clause at a splitting field, in datum form**: for a Čech class `M` over
227	`C_L`, admitting an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` is exactly
228	`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` of any datum presenting `M` — as a class over the base `L` itself,
229	where `relCurveMap C L L` is the identity comparison.
230	
231	Note the datum lives over the *field* `L` as base ring, which is the affine base the
232	engine's `PrimeSpectrum L` has a unique point of; that is why the fibre reading and the
233	base reading coincide here. -/
234	theorem exists_witness_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_datum
235	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
236	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C L π) {M : (relCurve C L).CechPic}
237	    (hD : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass
238	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M) :
239	    (∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
240	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M
241	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
242	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1))
243	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
244	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hD]
245	
246	/-- **Upward closure of the witness clause along a separable extension of the splitting
247	field** — the substantive half of the (a-amendment)'s "some (equivalently every)".
248	
249	If a Čech class `M` over `C_L` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`, then
250	so does its base change to any finite separable `L'/L`.  This is what makes two splittings
251	of the same plus class comparable: pass to a common separable extension and compare there,
252	rather than comparing the two splittings directly.
253	
254	Proof: present `M` by a datum `D` over `L` (`exists_cechPicClass_eq`); the witness clause at
255	`L` is `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L`, which transfers to `L'` by the co-owned separable
256	invariance `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`
257	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:157` — itself resting only on faithful flatness of a field
258	extension, so separability is packaging, not content). -/
259	theorem exists_witness_of_separable_extension (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
260	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
261	    {L' : Type u} [Field L'] [Algebra k L'] [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower k L L']
262	    [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
263	    (h : ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
264	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
265	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
266	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
267	    ∃ W' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left).CurveDivisor,
268	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L' W' = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L') M
269	        ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
270	            ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left.divisorSheaf L' W') 1) := by
271	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (B := L) (π := π) M
272	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
273	  -- the witness clause at `L` is the datum predicate at `L`: `relCurveMap C L L` acts as
274	  -- the identity comparison on classes, since it is `Spec` of the identity algebra map.
275	  have hid : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass := by
276	    have : relCurveMap C L L = 𝟙 (relCurve C L) := by
277	      rw [relCurveMap]
278	      have hom : overSpecMap (k := k) L L = 𝟙 (overSpec k L) :=
279	        Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simp)
280	      rw [hom, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id]
281	      rfl
282	    rw [this, Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
283	    rfl
284	  have hL : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := ⟨W, by rw [hid, hD, hW], hW1⟩
285	  -- transfer along the separable extension, then read it back as a witness clause
286	  obtain ⟨W', hW', hW1'⟩ :=
287	    (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable L L').mp hL
288	  exact ⟨W', by rw [hW', hD], hW1'⟩
289	
290	/-! ## Naturality — the half CHART-U(b) transport (i) consumes -/
291	
292	/-- **`chartLocus` is compatible with restriction of the class**: the twist commutes with
293	`picEtMap`, so restricting `λ` along a morphism of tests restricts the twisted family too.
294	
295	This is `sigmaFamily_natural` + `thetaFamily_natural` and nothing else; it is stated
296	separately because transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 (the descent-preimage step) is exactly
297	this identity read at the field point of a point over the source. -/
298	theorem picEtMap_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
299	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) :
300	    picEtMap C f (chartTwist C m Z T lam)
301	      = chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam) := by
302	  rw [chartTwist, chartTwist, map_mul, map_inv, map_mul, map_pow,
303	    sigmaFamily_natural, thetaFamily_natural]
304	
305	/-- **`chartLocus` pulls back into `chartLocus`** — transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6, in the
306	form the assembly consumes.
307	
308	For `f : T' ⟶ T` and `t : T'.left`, membership of `t` in the pulled-back locus and of `f t`
309	in the original are the *same* condition on the *same* twisted class, read at two fields:
310	`κ(t)` and `κ(f t)`, with `κ(f t) → κ(t)` the induced extension (`testPointFieldMap`).  So
311	the transport is exactly the invariance of `IsSplitWitness` under that extension.
312	
313	**This lemma proves nothing on its own — it is an interface, and its proof is `hinv`.**  Said
314	plainly so that no lane cites it as if transport (i) were discharged.  What it *does* is fix
315	the exact shape of the obligation and put the burden where it belongs: on the morphism `f`,
316	via the field extension `κ(f t) → κ(t)` it induces, rather than hidden inside the locus.  The
317	tree's landed invariance (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`) discharges `hinv` when
318	that extension is separable — which is the étale-carrier case the (b-amendment) needs, and is
319	*not* automatic for an arbitrary morphism of tests.  The residue between the two is why
320	`hinv` is a hypothesis and not a `rw`. -/
321	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp (m : ℕ)
322	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
323	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t : T'.left)
324	    (hinv : IsSplitWitness C
325	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))
326	      → IsSplitWitness C
327	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam)))) :
328	    f.left.base t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam
329	      → t ∈ chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C f lam) :=
330	  hinv

9	/-!
10	# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
17	fibre is a single point.
18	
19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
21	
22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
23	
24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
26	
27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
39	
40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
43	
44	## Main declarations
45	
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
47	  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at
48	  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of
51	  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any
52	  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart
54	  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of
55	  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the
56	  source).
57	-/

76	
77	/-- **Open immersions transfer through yoneda**: for an open immersion of schemes

90	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=
91	  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›

95	/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**
96	
97	`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor
98	scheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the
99	yoneda image of the open inclusion.
100	
101	The point of restricting is that the unrestricted Abel map is *not* an open immersion of
102	presheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where
103	the fibre is a single point is.  This definition is neutral about which open `V` is; the
104	chart-locus choice enters only in the certificate. -/
105	def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
106	    (V : X.Opens) : yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
107	  yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f
108	
109	/-- **The composition half of the `hf` certificate**: a restriction of an open immersion of
110	presheaves along an open immersion is again one.
111	
112	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda`, which is stable under
113	composition (`MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`, needing `yoneda` full and
114	faithful and `IsOpenImmersion` stable under composition — all instances).  Together with
115	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` this discharges, for free and in full generality, the
116	part of C9b that is bookkeeping.
117	
118	What it does NOT discharge, and what is therefore the whole remaining content of C9b: the
119	hypothesis `hfV`.  For `f := abelSigmaChart` that hypothesis is FALSE for `V = ⊤` and is
120	expected to be true for `V = chartLocus` — it is CHART-U(c), whose proof needs the
121	uniqueness of the normalized effective representative (DAT-C GAP-2) and the classifier.  A
122	lane must not read this lemma as reducing C9b to plumbing; it isolates the plumbing so the
123	mathematics is visible. -/
124	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}}
125	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : X.Opens)
126	    (hfV : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
127	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V) :=
128	  MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
129	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map V.ι) hfV
130	
131	/-! ## CHART-U(c): the remaining obligation, pinned
132	
133	With the composition half discharged, `hf` for a restricted Abel chart reduces to a single
134	statement.  It is pinned here as a definition so that the gate has a name in Lean and not
135	only in a worksheet — the pattern `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.IsChartDatumPresentation` uses.
136	
137	**Its field-level input is available.**  DAT-C GAP-2 (Σ-UNIQ-fld) is *landed*:
138	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`
139	(`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`) — for effective `D`, `D'` with equal Čech class
140	and `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1`, `D' = D`.  (The `w4-datc` §0.3 GAP-2 row claimed no such lemma existed;
141	that claim was stale and is corrected there as of 2026-07-28.)  What CHART-U(c) still needs
142	beyond it is the *relative* statement — uniqueness in families over the locus — plus the
143	classifier `divRepClassifyZar`. -/
144	
145	variable (C π n) in
146	/-- **CHART-U(c), pinned**: the chart map is an open immersion of presheaves after restriction
147	to the locus where the fibre class has a unique effective representative.
148	
149	This is the whole remaining content of C9b's `hf`.  Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition
150	rather than proved, because its proof needs the *relative* form of GAP-2 over `chartLocus`
151	together with `divRepClassifyZar`; a lane that discharges it gets `hf` by feeding it to
152	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart`.
153	
154	Deliberately stated about `abelSigmaChart` and a *given* open `V`, rather than about
155	`chartLocus` directly: the openness of `chartLocus` is a separate obligation
156	(`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`), and keeping the two apart means neither has to wait for the
157	other. -/
158	def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
159	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
160	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
161	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
162	    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
163	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V)
164	
165	/-- The pinned obligation is exactly what `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` would
166	give from an unrestricted certificate — recorded so that no lane proves the same thing
167	twice, and so that the *reason* the unrestricted route is unavailable stays visible: the
168	hypothesis of that lemma is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`. -/
169	lemma isChartUniv_of_unrestricted {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
170	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
171	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
172	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
173	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
174	    (V : D.left.Opens)
175	    (h : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :
176	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
177	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V h
178	
179	/-! ## The structure morphism of a restricted chart -/
180	
181	/-- **The structure morphism of a restricted chart is the restriction of the structure
182	morphism.**  Hence the `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` hypothesis of
183	`JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited by every restriction: being locally of finite type is
184	local on the source, and an open immersion is locally of finite type.
185	
186	Concretely, for the Abel chart of a representation `rep` by `D` the unrestricted structure
187	morphism is `D.hom` (`chartHom_abelSigmaChart`, `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:212`), so a
188	restricted Abel chart over `V ⊆ D.left` has structure morphism `V.ι ≫ D.hom`. -/
189	lemma chartHom_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
190	    (V : X.Opens) {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
191	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => restrictChart f V) i
192	      = V.ι ≫ chartHom C (fun _ : ι => f) i := by
193	  change (yonedaEquiv (yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f)).1 = V.ι ≫ (yonedaEquiv f).1
194	  -- Both sides are the Σ-component of the universal element restricted along `V.ι`:
195	  -- the `Over.sigmaExtension` transition map precomposes the structure morphism, and
196	  -- `f`'s naturality moves the restriction across `f`.
197	  rw [yonedaEquiv_comp, yonedaEquiv_yoneda_map]
198	  have hnat := congrArg Sigma.fst
199	    (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (f.naturality (V.ι).op) (𝟙 X))
200	  refine hnat.trans ?_
201	  exact Over.sigmaExtension_map_fst (V.ι) _
202	
203	end
204	
205	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# CHART-U(b) gap-2, the chartLocus-free core — fibre-field invariance of witness
10	h¹-vanishing (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 transport (ii), I-0252 gap 2)
11	
12	CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii) (the "one `IsOpenMap` application", `Pic0ChartLocusOpen`
13	keystones 2/3) pushes the engine's open witness locus from the étale carrier `Spec B`
14	down to the test base `Spec A`.  Its remaining mathematical content (I-0252 gap 2) is
15	the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the preimage of the base locus with the
16	carrier locus: for a prime `q` of the carrier over `p`, the residue-field extension
17	`κ(q)/κ(p)` is separable (étale/étale-plus carrier) and must **preserve** the witness
18	h¹-vanishing of the fibre class.
19	
20	That content is `chartLocus`-free (I-0252's phrasing through the still-undefined
21	`chartLocus`, DAT-C C9, is pure plumbing on top) and is landed here in the **witness
22	form** `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`
23	(`Pic0ChartLocusOpen`) uses.  The heart is a single module fact:
24	
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff` — for an `S`-module `H`
26	  and a field extension `L → L'` in the `S`-tower, `H ⊗[S] L` is subsingleton iff
27	  `H ⊗[S] L'` is.  Going up is `0 ⊗ = 0`; coming down is the faithful flatness of the
28	  (nonzero) field extension.  **Separability is not needed** — every field extension is
29	  faithfully flat; it is the geometric packaging (étale carrier) that makes the residue
30	  extensions separable, not the transfer.
31	
32	Read through the two-way datum dictionary
33	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6) — under
34	which the witness predicate at a field `L` is exactly the engine's complex-form fibre
35	condition `Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L)` — this gives:
36	
37	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing` — the field-parametrised witness
38	  predicate; for `L = κ(q)` it is membership of `q` in the keystone-1 locus.
39	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` — **the gap-2
40	  core**: witness h¹-vanishing of `D` at `L` transfers to and from `L'` for any field
41	  extension `L → L'` in the `k`/`B` tower.
42	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable` — the separable
43	  specialisation the CHART-U(b) consumer names (`Algebra.IsSeparable`).
44	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq` — the fixed-
45	  field class-intrinsicity (V1a): the witness predicate depends only on the mapped fibre
46	  class, so two data with equal fibre class at `L` have the same predicate.
47	
48	## What the CHART-U(b) / C9 assembly consumes and the residual (I-0252 gap 2)
49	
50	The `comap`-preimage identity keystone 3 needs, `comap f ⁻¹'(chartLocus_A) = locus_B`,
51	reduces pointwise (for `q` over `p`, `κ(q)/κ(p)` separable) to two links:
52	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` (the `κ(p) → κ(q)` field transfer, landed
53	here) composed with `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq` at the fixed field
54	`κ(q)` (landed here).  The **residual** is the input to the latter — the shifted-datum
55	class identity `map (relCurveMap … κ(q)) D_A.cechPicClass = map (relCurveMap … κ(q))
56	D_B.cechPicClass` (I-0252 gap 1, the Σ/θ naturality) — and the `chartLocus` definition
57	itself (DAT-C C9).  Both are divRep/C9-gated; neither is a mathematical wall on the
58	invariance itself, which is complete.
59	-/

81	/-! ## The module-theoretic core -/
82	
83	/-- **Base change of a module along a field extension preserves triviality**: for an
84	`S`-module `H` and a field extension `L → L'` inside the `S`-tower, `H ⊗[S] L` is
85	subsingleton iff `H ⊗[S] L'` is.
86	
87	Going up is `0 ⊗ = 0`; coming down is the faithful flatness of the (nonzero) field
88	extension `L → L'` (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_triviality`), read across the
89	base-change-in-stages equivalence `(TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange)`.
90	**Separability is not used** — every field extension is faithfully flat. -/
91	theorem subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff
92	    {S L L' H : Type u} [CommRing S] [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra S L] [Algebra S L']
93	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower S L L'] [AddCommGroup H] [Module S H] :
94	    Subsingleton (H ⊗[S] L) ↔ Subsingleton (H ⊗[S] L') := by
95	  have e := TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange S L L' L' H
96	  rw [(TensorProduct.comm S H L).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr,
97	      (TensorProduct.comm S H L').toEquiv.subsingleton_congr,
98	      ← e.toEquiv.subsingleton_congr]
99	  exact ⟨fun _ => inferInstance,
100	    fun _ => Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_triviality L L' (L ⊗[S] H)⟩
101	
102	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
103	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
104	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
105	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
106	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

108	/-! ## The witness predicate as a function of the fibre field -/
109	
110	/-- **The chart-membership witness predicate at a field `L`** — the field-parametrised
111	form of the set of `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`
112	(`Pic0ChartLocusOpen`): the fibre class of `D` at `L` admits an effective witness divisor
113	with vanishing `H¹`.  For `L = q.asIdeal.ResidueField` this is definitionally membership
114	of `q` in the keystone-1 witness locus. -/
115	def BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
116	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L] [IsScalarTower k B L] : Prop :=
117	  ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
118	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W
119	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass
120	      ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
121	
122	/-- The witness predicate is the engine's complex-form fibre condition
123	`Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L)`, via the two-way datum dictionary
124	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6). -/
125	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton
126	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
127	    [IsScalarTower k B L] :
128	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L) :=
129	  (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness L).symm
130	
131	/-! ## The fibre-field invariance (the gap-2 core) -/
132	
133	/-- **CHART-U(b) gap-2 core — fibre-field invariance of witness h¹-vanishing**: for a
134	pinned datum `D` over the affine base `B` and a field extension `L → L'` inside the
135	`k`/`B` tower (the residue-field seam `κ(p) → κ(q)` of a carrier map `comap f`), the
136	witness h¹-vanishing of `D` at `L` transfers to and from `L'`.
137	
138	Both sides are, via the datum dictionary, `Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] ·)`, and
139	that transfers along the (faithfully flat) field extension `L → L'`
140	(`subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff`).  In particular this covers the separable
141	residue-field extensions of an étale/étale-plus carrier map. -/
142	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
143	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
144	    (L L' : Type u) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra k L] [Algebra k L']
145	    [Algebra B L] [Algebra B L'] [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B L']
146	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower B L L'] :
147	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L' := by
148	  rw [D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L,
149	      D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L']
150	  exact subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff
151	
152	/-- **The separable specialisation the CHART-U(b) transport (ii) names** (I-0252 gap 2):
153	for a **separable** residue-field extension `L → L'` (`Algebra.IsSeparable`, the case of
154	an étale/étale-plus carrier map), witness h¹-vanishing of `D` transfers between `L` and
155	`L'`.  Separability is recorded to name the intended consumer; the transfer holds for any
156	field extension (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`). -/
157	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable
158	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
159	    (L L' : Type u) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra k L] [Algebra k L']
160	    [Algebra B L] [Algebra B L'] [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B L']
161	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower B L L'] [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] :
162	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L' :=
163	  D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension L L'
164	
165	/-! ## Fixed-field class-intrinsicity (the other half the `comap` identity needs) -/
166	
167	/-- **Class-intrinsicity of the witness predicate at a fixed field** (V1a): the witness
168	h¹-vanishing predicate depends only on the mapped fibre class
169	`Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass`, so two data — over possibly
170	different bases `B`, `B'` — whose fibre classes at `L` agree have the same witness
171	predicate at `L`.
172	
173	Together with `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` (the `κ(p) → κ(q)` transfer)
174	this is exactly what the CHART-U(b) `comap`-preimage identity reduces to at C9-time; the
175	one residual input is the shifted-datum class identity of I-0252 gap 1 (the Σ/θ
176	naturality), which is divRep-gated. -/
177	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq
178	    {B' : Type u} [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B']
179	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (D' : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B' π)
180	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra B' L]
181	    [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B' L]
182	    (hcl : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass
183	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B' L) D'.cechPicClass) :
184	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D'.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
185	  simp only [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hcl]

9	/-!
10	# Field points of a general test from points of its space — CHART-U(a) input 0
11	
12	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 freezes `chartLocus c λ` as a **subset of a general
13	test** `T`: a set of *points* `t : T.left`, at each of which one reads the fibre class of
14	`λ` at the residue field `κ(t)`.  `informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 co-signs it and
15	lists three missing inputs (the shifted-datum constructor, the split predicate, the
16	descent/étale-image transports).
17	
18	**There is a fourth, prior to all three, and it is why nothing in the tree implements
19	`chartLocus`.**  The two vocabularies the definition has to join do not meet anywhere:
20	
21	* every witness/vanishing predicate in the tree is indexed by a prime of an **affine**
22	  base — `q : PrimeSpectrum B`, fibre field `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`
23	  (`Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:80`, `Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean:82`,
24	  `DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:363`);
25	* every *class* is evaluated at a field point only through a **morphism**
26	  `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` for an abstract field `K` (`degAt`, `Pic0Functor.lean:54`;
27	  `pic0Subgroup`, `:107`).
28	
29	Nothing converts a point of `T.left` into either.  This file is that conversion, and it
30	is deliberately kept free of the chart layer: no `chartLocus`, no `θ`, no `Σ`, no
31	`divRep`.
32	
33	## Main declarations
34	
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointField t` — the residue field `κ(t)` of a point of
36	  `T.left`, as a `k`-algebra (`Scheme.residueField`, with the `k`-algebra structure
37	  pulled back along the structure morphism).
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint t` — **the bridge**: the field point
39	  `overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ T` supported at `t`.  Built from mathlib's
40	  `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, whose triangle over `Spec k` is the `Over` datum.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint_base` — it really is supported at `t`: the unique
42	  point of `Spec κ(t)` maps to `t`.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint_comp` — **naturality**, the law every well-definedness
44	  argument downstream runs on: for `f : T' ⟶ T` and `t : T'.left`, the field point of `t`
45	  followed by `f` is the field point of `f t`, up to the residue-field extension
46	  `κ(f t) → κ(t)` that `f` induces.  Stated as a commuting square rather than an equality
47	  of morphisms out of one object, because the two sides have different sources.
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointAffine` — the affine comparison: on `overSpec k A` the
49	  field point of a prime `q` is the residue-field point of `q`, so every affine-indexed
50	  predicate of the tree can be read through `testPoint`.
51	
52	## Why the affine-chart route is *not* the definition of record
53	
54	The obvious route (pick an affine open `U ∋ t`, use `q := U.2.primeIdealOf t` and
55	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`, `PicEtUnit.lean:61`) needs a well-definedness lemma across the
56	choice of `U` before it can define anything.  Mathlib's `fromSpecResidueField` is already
57	canonical, so the chart-independence is *free* here and the chart comparison becomes a
58	lemma (`testPointField_affineOpen_iso`) instead of a side condition.  That is the whole
59	reason this file is short.
60	-/
61

76	noncomputable section

78	/-! ## The residue field of a point of a test object -/
79	
80	/-- **The residue field of a point of a test object**, as a `k`-algebra: the scheme
81	residue field `κ(t)` of `Scheme.residueField`, with the `k`-algebra structure obtained by
82	transporting the structure morphism `T ⟶ Spec k` through `Spec.preimage`.
83	
84	This is the field at which the fibre of a class over `T` is read at `t`.  It is a bare
85	`Type u` field with a `k`-algebra instance, which is exactly the shape `degAt` and
86	`pic0Subgroup` quantify over. -/
87	def testPointField {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left) : Type u :=
88	  T.left.residueField t
89	
90	instance instFieldTestPointField {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left) :
91	    Field (testPointField t) :=
92	  inferInstanceAs (Field (T.left.residueField t))
93	
94	/-- The `k`-algebra structure on `κ(t)`: `Spec.preimage` of the composite
95	`Spec κ(t) ⟶ T.left ⟶ Spec k`. -/
96	instance instAlgebraTestPointField {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left) :
97	    Algebra k (testPointField t) :=
98	  (Spec.preimage (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ T.hom)).hom.toAlgebra
99	
100	lemma algebraMap_testPointField {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left) :
101	    algebraMap k (testPointField t)
102	      = (Spec.preimage (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ T.hom)).hom :=
103	  rfl
104	
105	/-! ## The affine case: the test algebra also acts
106	
107	Over an affine test `overSpec k A` the residue field of a point is a `κ(t)`-algebra over `A`
108	as well as over `k`, and the two structures form a tower.  This is what the engine-facing
109	predicates of the tree require — `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing` takes
110	`[Algebra B L]` and `[IsScalarTower k B L]` — so without these two instances the
111	`testPoint`-indexed loci and the `PrimeSpectrum`-indexed loci cannot even be compared.
112	
113	Both come from the same source as the `k`-structure: `Spec.preimage` of the composite
114	`Spec κ(t) ⟶ Spec A`, which for an affine test is the structure morphism itself. -/
115	
116	section Affine
117	
118	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
119	
120	/-- The `A`-algebra structure on the residue field of a point of an affine test: the
121	`Spec.preimage` of `Spec κ(t) ⟶ Spec A`.  (Over an affine test the carrier of the test object
122	*is* `Spec A`, so the composite is `fromSpecResidueField` alone.) -/
123	instance instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
124	    Algebra A (testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
125	  (Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)).hom.toAlgebra
126	
127	lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
128	    algebraMap A (testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
129	      = (Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)).hom :=
130	  rfl
131	
132	/-- **The tower `k → A → κ(t)`** on an affine test.  `Spec` of the tower identity is the
133	factorisation of `Spec κ(t) ⟶ Spec k` through `Spec A`, which is the `Over` triangle of the
134	affine test object — the same identity `isScalarTower_fieldPointAlgebra`
135	(`Picard/Pic0Theta.lean:358`) proves for an abstract field point, here at the canonical
136	residue-field point. -/
137	instance instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
138	    IsScalarTower k A (testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
139	  refine IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' ?_
140	  -- Both algebra maps are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`; `Spec.preimage`
141	  -- is a bijection on homs, so it suffices to compare the two morphisms, and there the
142	  -- identity is the `Over` triangle of the affine test object: `(overSpec k A).hom` is by
143	  -- definition `Spec.map (algebraMap k A)`.
144	  have hcomp : ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ (overSpec k A).hom)
145	      = (overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t
146	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) := rfl
147	  -- `Spec.preimage` is injective on the composite, and the composite identity is `hcomp`.
148	  have hw := congrArg (fun f => (Spec.preimage f).hom) hcomp
149	  have hsplit : (Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t
150	        ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).hom
151	      = (algebraMap A (testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).comp
152	          (algebraMap k A) := by
153	    have : ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t
154	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))
155	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)
156	            ≫ Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)) := by
157	      rw [Spec.map_comp, Spec.map_preimage]
158	      rfl
159	    rw [this, Spec.preimage_map]
160	    rfl
161	  exact hw.trans hsplit
162	
163	end Affine
164	
165	/-! ## The field point -/
166	
167	/-- **The bridge: a point of `T.left` as a field point of `T`.**
168	
169	`t : T.left` names the test object morphism `overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ T` whose carrier is
170	mathlib's canonical `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField` and whose triangle over `Spec k` holds
171	by the very definition of the `k`-algebra structure on `κ(t)`.
172	
173	This is the missing input 0 of CHART-U(a): with it, `{t : T.left | P (fibre of λ at
174	κ(t))}` is a legal `Set T.left` for any predicate `P` on classes over a field, and that
175	is what `chartLocus` is. -/
176	def testPoint {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left) :
177	    overSpec k (testPointField t) ⟶ T :=
178	  Over.homMk (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)
179	    (Spec.map_preimage (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ T.hom)).symm
180	
181	@[simp]
182	lemma testPoint_left {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left) :
183	    (testPoint t).left = T.left.fromSpecResidueField t :=
184	  rfl
185	
186	/-- **The field point is supported at the point it came from**: the unique point of
187	`Spec κ(t)` maps to `t`.  (`Spec` of a field has a unique point, so this pins the support
188	completely.) -/
189	@[simp]
190	lemma testPoint_base {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left)
191	    (s : (overSpec k (testPointField t)).left) :
192	    (testPoint t).left.base s = t :=
193	  Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply t s
194	
195	/-! ## Naturality along a morphism of tests
196	
197	The law every downstream well-definedness argument runs on.  A morphism `f : T' ⟶ T`
198	does not send the field point of `t` to the field point of `f t` on the nose — the two
199	have *different sources*, `Spec κ(t)` and `Spec κ(f t)`.  What is true, and what the
200	transports of `w4-datb` §1.6 use, is that the square through the induced residue-field
201	extension `κ(f t) → κ(t)` commutes. -/
202	
203	/-- **The residue-field extension a morphism of tests induces at a point**, as a
204	`k`-algebra map `κ(f t) → κ(t)`.  This is `Scheme.Hom.residueFieldMap` with its
205	`k`-algebra structure read off; it is the extension along which every fibre-field
206	predicate has to be invariant for a locus over `T` to pull back to one over `T'`. -/
207	def testPointFieldMap {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left) :
208	    CommRingCat.of (testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t))
209	      ⟶ CommRingCat.of (testPointField (T := T') t) :=
210	  f.left.residueFieldMap t
211	
212	/-- The residue-field extension of `testPointFieldMap`, as an algebra structure: `κ(t)` is
213	a `κ(f t)`-algebra.  This is the shape the fibre-field invariance lemmas of
214	`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean` consume (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
215	takes `[Algebra L L']`). -/
216	@[reducible]
217	def testPointFieldAlgebra {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left) :
218	    Algebra (testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t)) (testPointField (T := T') t) :=
219	  (testPointFieldMap f t).hom.toAlgebra
220	
221	/-- **The naturality square of the bridge**: the field point of `t : T'.left` composed
222	with `f` is the field point of `f t` precomposed with `Spec` of the residue-field
223	extension.  Both sides are morphisms `overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ T` in the slice.
224	
225	This is `Scheme.Hom.SpecMap_residueFieldMap_fromSpecResidueField` in the over category,
226	and it is the only law CHART-U(b)'s transports (i)/(ii) need from this file. -/
227	lemma testPoint_comp_left {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left) :
228	    (testPoint t).left ≫ f.left
229	      = Spec.map (testPointFieldMap f t) ≫ (testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)).left :=
230	  (f.left.SpecMap_residueFieldMap_fromSpecResidueField t).symm
231	
232	end
233	
234	end Over
235	
236	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# DAT-C GAP-1: the inverse cocycle datum (the shifted-datum constructor's first half)
10	
11	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §0.3 GAP-1 (Σ-INV) and `informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md`
12	§1.6 both name the same missing input, and both name it as the reason the CHART-U(b) twist
13	"has no route": **there is no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.inv` and no tensor/`mul` anywhere in
14	the tree**, so a datum for a class cannot be turned into a datum for its inverse or for a
15	product.  Every landed datum built from a divisor family is the *twisted ideal*
16	`thetaIdealDatum a` of class `θᵃ·[d]⁻¹` (`Picard/DivisorThetaDatum.lean:362`), i.e. the
17	tree can only produce data whose class carries a built-in inverse it cannot remove.
18	
19	This file supplies the inverse half, exactly as GAP-1 pins it:
20	
21	> `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.invDatum` (same pieces, units `(D.unit i j)⁻¹`; the cocycle law inverts
22	> termwise), with `cechPicClass_inv = (cechPicClass)⁻¹`.
23	
24	## Main declarations
25	
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.invDatum` — the inverse datum: the *same* cover data
27	  (so the same pieces, the same partitions — nothing about the cover changes), with every
28	  transition unit inverted.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isGluingCocycle_inv` — the cocycle law for the
30	  inverted units.  This is where the mathematical content sits, and it is small but not
31	  vacuous: the cocycle identity `g_ij · g_jl = g_il` inverts to
32	  `g_ij⁻¹ · g_jl⁻¹ = g_il⁻¹` only because the overlap section rings are **commutative**, so
33	  the inverse of a product is the product of inverses in either order.  In the
34	  non-commutative setting the correct law would be `(g_jl · g_ij)⁻¹` and the statement would
35	  need a transpose.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.inv_inv` — the involution.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.pieces_inv` / `unit_inv_coe` — the two `rfl`
38	  anchors consumers unfold through.
39	
40	## What this does and does not unblock
41	
42	It gives the twist a *route*: a datum for `μ` and the θ/Σ layer's datum now compose to a
43	datum for `μ·θ^m·(−Σ)` as soon as the second half of GAP-1 — the `mul`/tensor of two data
44	on a *common refinement* of their covers — is available.  That second half is genuinely
45	larger than this one (it needs a refinement of two basic-open covers and a comparison of
46	the two `cechPicClass` readings on it), and it is NOT in this file; see the closing note.
47	
48	`cechPicClass_inv` is likewise NOT here.  Stating it needs the subordinated-cocycle
49	`inv_unitsEvInf`-style calculus that `DivSchemeFibreH1.lean:63-66` uses *privately*, and
50	lifting that to a public lemma is its own brick.  What is here is the carrier plus its
51	cocycle law — the part GAP-1 says has no avatar at all, and the part every route needs
52	first.
53	-/

68	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
69	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
70	
71	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
72	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
73	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
74	
75	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
76	
77	/-! ## The cocycle law inverts termwise -/
78	
79	/-- **The inverted transition units satisfy the cocycle law** (GAP-1's "the cocycle law
80	inverts termwise").
81	
82	The two clauses:
83	* normalization — `(g i i)⁻¹ = 1⁻¹ = 1`, by `unit_self` and `inv_one`;
84	* the cocycle identity — apply `resHom` (a ring hom, hence unit-preserving) to
85	  `g_ij · g_jl = g_il` and invert.  The step that makes this work is **commutativity** of
86	  the triple-overlap section ring: `(a·b)⁻¹ = a⁻¹·b⁻¹` needs `a·b = b·a`.  Over a
87	  non-commutative base the correct inverse cocycle would carry a transposed index pair.
88	
89	Stated for an arbitrary family of transition units rather than for a datum, so that the
90	θ/Σ layer can reuse it without building a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` first. -/
91	theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsGluingCocycle.inv {X : Scheme.{u}} {J : Type u}
92	    {U : J → X.Opens} {g : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ}
93	    (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g) :
94	    Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U (fun i j => (g i j)⁻¹) where
95	  unit_self i := by
96	    have h : (g i i) = 1 := Units.ext (by rw [hc.unit_self i]; rfl)
97	    rw [h, inv_one]
98	    rfl
99	  mul_res i j l := by
100	    -- Abbreviate the three restriction maps to the triple overlap.
101	    set rij := X.resHom (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l ≤ U i ⊓ U j) with hrij
102	    set rjl := X.resHom (gluedInclCoc U (U i) j l) with hrjl
103	    set ril := X.resHom (gluedInclSnd U (U i) j l) with hril
104	    -- `resHom` sends a unit and its inverse to a mutually inverse pair, so the image of
105	    -- an inverse is characterised by `mul_eq_one`.  Record that for each of the three.
106	    have hu : ∀ {V W : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ W) (a : Γ(X, W)ˣ),
107	        X.resHom h (Units.val a⁻¹) * X.resHom h (Units.val a) = 1 := by
108	      intro V W h a
109	      rw [← map_mul]
110	      have : ((a⁻¹ : Γ(X, W)ˣ) : Γ(X, W)) * ((a : Γ(X, W)ˣ) : Γ(X, W)) = 1 :=
111	        a.inv_mul
112	      rw [this, map_one]
113	    -- Multiply the target by the uninverted cocycle identity and cancel.
114	    have key := hc.mul_res i j l
115	    rw [← hrij, ← hrjl, ← hril] at key
116	    have hcancel : (rij (Units.val (g i j)⁻¹)
117	          * rjl (Units.val (g j l)⁻¹))
118	        * (rij (Units.val (g i j)) * rjl (Units.val (g j l))) = 1 := by
119	      calc (rij (Units.val (g i j)⁻¹) * rjl (Units.val (g j l)⁻¹))
120	            * (rij (Units.val (g i j)) * rjl (Units.val (g j l)))
121	          = (rij (Units.val (g i j)⁻¹) * rij (Units.val (g i j)))
122	            * (rjl (Units.val (g j l)⁻¹)
123	                * rjl (Units.val (g j l))) := by ring
124	        _ = 1 := by rw [hu, hu, one_mul]
125	    -- Both sides are the inverse of the same element of the commutative monoid, hence equal.
126	    rw [key] at hcancel
127	    have hril_inv : ril (Units.val (g i l)⁻¹) * ril (Units.val (g i l)) = 1 :=
128	      hu _ _
129	    calc rij (Units.val (g i j)⁻¹) * rjl (Units.val (g j l)⁻¹)
130	        = (rij (Units.val (g i j)⁻¹) * rjl (Units.val (g j l)⁻¹))
131	            * (ril (Units.val (g i l))
132	                * ril (Units.val (g i l)⁻¹)) := by
133	          rw [mul_comm (ril (Units.val (g i l))), hril_inv, mul_one]
134	      _ = (rij (Units.val (g i j)⁻¹) * rjl (Units.val (g j l)⁻¹)
135	            * ril (Units.val (g i l))) * ril (Units.val (g i l)⁻¹) := by
136	          ring
137	      _ = ril (Units.val (g i l)⁻¹) := by rw [hcancel, one_mul]
138	
139	/-! ## The inverse datum -/
140	
141	/-- **GAP-1: the inverse cocycle datum.**  Same cover data — same pieces, same partitions,
142	same index — with every transition unit inverted.  The cocycle law is
143	`Scheme.IsGluingCocycle.inv`.
144	
145	This is the constructor `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §0.3 GAP-1 pins and reports as
146	having no avatar anywhere in the tree.  With it, a datum for a class `μ` yields one for
147	`μ⁻¹`, which is what the `(−Σ)` and `(θ^m)⁻¹` factors of the chart twist
148	(`chartTwist`, `Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean`) need in order to have a datum-level route at
149	all: every landed datum built from a divisor family is `thetaIdealDatum a` of class
150	`θᵃ·[d]⁻¹`, i.e. carries a built-in inverse the tree previously could not remove. -/
151	noncomputable def invDatum (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π where
152	  toBasicOpenCoverData := D.toBasicOpenCoverData
153	  unit i j := (D.unit i j)⁻¹
154	  isGluingCocycle := D.isGluingCocycle.inv
155	
156	@[simp]
157	lemma invDatum_toBasicOpenCoverData (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
158	    D.invDatum.toBasicOpenCoverData = D.toBasicOpenCoverData :=
159	  rfl
160	
161	/-- The inverse datum has the same pieces — the cover is untouched, only the transitions
162	move.  Consumers that reason about supports or coverings may therefore reuse every
163	piece-level fact of `D` verbatim. -/
164	@[simp]
165	lemma pieces_invDatum (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
166	    D.invDatum.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces = D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces :=
167	  rfl
168	
169	@[simp]
170	lemma unit_invDatum (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (i j : D.toBasicOpenCoverData.index) :
171	    D.invDatum.unit i j = (D.unit i j)⁻¹ :=
172	  rfl
173	
174	/-- **The inversion is an involution.**  The cover data is carried through unchanged and
175	the units invert twice, so this is the `Units` involution applied pointwise. -/
176	@[simp]
177	lemma invDatum_invDatum (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) : D.invDatum.invDatum = D := by
178	  cases D with
179	  | mk cover unit hc =>
180	      congr 1
181	
182	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

8	/-!
9	# CHART-U(b) — datum-level openness of the chart-membership (witness) locus
10	(`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3)
11	
12	The affine-level heart of the shared CHART-U(b) brick, stated directly on a pinned
13	basic-open cocycle datum in the **witness form** the `chartLocus` predicate uses.
14	
15	For a datum `D` over an affine base `B`, the locus of primes `q` of `B` at which the
16	fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` admits an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`
17	is Zariski-open in `Spec B`.  This is the single sanctioned openness mechanism of the
18	campaign (`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, Noetherian-free — dat-d §3.5) read
19	through the two-way datum dictionary of C1
20	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness`,
21	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-6): the engine open is the complex-form fibre
22	condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`, and the dictionary rewrites it,
23	pointwise and class-intrinsically, as the effective-witness/h¹-vanishing condition.
24	
25	Role in the CHART-U(b) chain (the two unlanded links of §5 risk 1):
26	
27	* **the shifted-datum constructor (link 1):** over the étale carrier `B` the plus
28	  class collapses to an honest Čech class; twisted by the theta layer and DAT-C's
29	  GAP-1 inverse datum into the `λθᵐ(Σ-shift)⁻¹` class, then extracted
30	  (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) to a datum `D`.  The output of
31	  that link is exactly a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` — the input of the theorem
32	  below, whose witness set is then the `chartLocus`-over-`B`.
33	* **the étale-image openness transport (link 2):** the locus over the test base `A`
34	  is the image, under the (open, surjective) étale carrier map `Spec B → Spec A`, of
35	  the open locus this theorem produces — carried to `A` by mathlib's
36	  `IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap`/`IsQuotientMap.isOpen_preimage` once the fibre-field
37	  invariance identifies the preimage.
38	
39	The theorem is class-intrinsic (any datum in the class has the same witness set, by
40	(V1a)), so a change of extracted representative is free.
41	-/

69	/-- **CHART-U(b), the datum-level witness-locus openness** (`w4-datc` §3.3 step (3)):
70	for a pinned basic-open cocycle datum `D` over the affine base `B`, the locus of primes

106	away pieces, over `Spec (Localization.Away f)`).  CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii)
107	(`w4-datb` §1.6, "the Kleiman tex 2204-2244 step, now one `IsOpenMap` application")

      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) →

        (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
        Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) from
    H e W hdeg h1
  intro e
  induction e with
  | zero =>
    intro W hdeg h1
    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
    refine ⟨0, le_refl 0, by rw [CurveDivisor.deg_zero, Nat.cast_zero], ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro x hx hne
      exact (hne (CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero hx)).elim
    · rw [sub_zero]
      push_cast at hanchor
      omega
    · rw [sub_zero]
      exact h1
  | succ e ih =>
    intro W hdeg h1
    -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) = e + 2 > 0` by the rank anchor
    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
    have hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) := by
      push_cast at hanchor
      omega
    -- an admissible non-base point and the exact drop there
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfW, hf, hnb⟩ :=
      exists_admissible_nonbase_point P hdense hPcl W hpos
    obtain ⟨hdrop, h1'⟩ :=
      h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase W h1 hx (hPdeg x hxP) hfW hf hnb
############ SepPointsDense

/-- **COV-3, density of base-changed rational points** (★ B-2 keystone, worksheet
§1.5): over a separably closed base field `k`, for every field `L ⊇ k` and every
nonempty open `W` of the relative curve `C_L = relCurve C L`, some `k`-rational point
of `C` base-changes into `W`.

Route: pick an affine chart `U` of `C.left` under a point of `W`; its preimage chart of
`C_L` is affine with sections `Γ(U) ⊗_k L` (`Over.sectionsBaseChange`); a basic open
`D(f) ⊆ W` of the chart has a nonzero coordinate `a` in an `L`-basis
(`exists_algHom_tensorPointEval_ne_zero`); `D(a)` is nonempty in the reduced curve, and
DAT-P (`Over.exists_rationalPoint_mem`) supplies a rational point there whose base
change evaluates `f` to a nonzero element of `L`
(`gammaSpecIso_appLE_sectionsBaseChange`), hence lies in `D(f) ⊆ W`. -/
theorem Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints [IsSepClosed k]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsIntegral C.left]
    (W : (relCurve C L).Opens) (hW : (W : Set (relCurve C L)).Nonempty) :
    ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left) (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) ∈ W := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨z, hzW⟩ := hW
  -- an affine chart of `C.left` under `z`, and its affine preimage chart of `C_L`
  obtain ⟨U, hU, hxU, -⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset
    (X := C.left) (U := ⊤) (x := (fst C (overSpec k L)).left.base z) trivial
  haveI : IsAffineHom (fst C (overSpec k L)).left :=
    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsAffineHom)
      (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k L)).flip
      (isAffineHom_of_isAffine (overSpec k L).hom)
  have hV : IsAffineOpen ((fst C (overSpec k L)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U) :=
    hU.preimage (fst C (overSpec k L)).left
  have hzV : z ∈ (fst C (overSpec k L)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U := hxU
  -- a basic open of the chart inside `W` around `z`
  obtain ⟨f, hfW, hzf⟩ := hV.exists_basicOpen_le
    (V := W ⊓ ((fst C (overSpec k L)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U)) ⟨z, ⟨hzW, hzV⟩⟩ hzV
  -- its tensor coordinates: `f` is nonzero, hence has a nonzero coordinate
  have hf0 : f ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    rw [h0, Scheme.basicOpen_zero] at hzf
    exact hzf
  have hF0 : (Over.sectionsBaseChange C L hU.isCompact hU.isQuasiSeparated).symm f
      ≠ 0 := fun h0 => hf0 (by
    rw [← (Over.sectionsBaseChange C L hU.isCompact hU.isQuasiSeparated).apply_symm_apply
      f, h0, map_zero])
  obtain ⟨a, ha0, hkey⟩ := exists_algHom_tensorPointEval_ne_zero hF0
  -- the coordinate's basic open is nonempty in the reduced curve; DAT-P fires there
  have hane : (C.left.basicOpen a : Set C.left).Nonempty := by
    by_contra h
    rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.not_nonempty_iff_eq_bot, basicOpen_eq_bot_iff] at h
    exact ha0 h
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpmem⟩ := Over.exists_rationalPoint_mem C (C.left.basicOpen a) hane
  have hple : ⊤ ≤ p ⁻¹ᵁ U :=
    top_le_preimage_of_closedPoint_mem p ((C.left.basicOpen_le a) hpmem)
  -- the base-changed point lies in the chart …
  have hqle : ⊤ ≤ Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp ⁻¹ᵁ
      ((fst C (overSpec k L)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U) := by
    intro y _
    change (fst C (overSpec k L)).left.base
